```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Maganda BA, Ngaimisi E, Kamuhabwa AAR, Aklillu E, Minzi OMS (2015). The influence of nevirapine and efavirenz-based anti-retroviral therapy on the pharmacokinetics of lumefantrine and anti-malarial dose recommendation in HIV-malaria co-treatment. *Malaria Journal* 14:179.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12936-015-0695-2>

Maganda 2015 studied lumefantrine in HIV-infected Tanzanian adults with
uncomplicated falciparum malaria who received the standard six-dose
artemether-lumefantrine (AL) course while on nevirapine (NVP)-based
antiretroviral therapy (ART), on efavirenz (EFV)-based ART, or not yet on
ART. The final model is a two-compartment model with first-order absorption
and an absorption lag time, allometric body-weight scaling (70 kg reference)
on the clearances and volumes, and an effect of each ART arm on relative
bioavailability: EFV lowers it to 0.42 and NVP raises it to 1.32 of the
control arm. The authors then simulated longer or higher-dose AL regimens for
patients on EFV.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Maganda_2015_lumefantrine")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

`r mod_ui$population$n_subjects` adults (NVP arm n = 128, EFV arm n = 66,
control arm n = 75) were enrolled at the Bagamoyo District Hospital HIV clinic,
Tanzania, between 2010 and 2012 (Maganda 2015 Methods and Table 1). Arm median
ages were 38-43 years (range 19-67), median weights 55-58 kg, and 52-80% of
each arm was female. Patients on ART had taken NVP 200 mg twice daily or EFV
600 mg at night for at least two months. AL (480 mg lumefantrine per dose) was
given at 0, 8, 24, 36, 48 and 60 h with milk, and 1,514 sparse plasma samples
were taken from the fifth dose to day 14.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two compartments, first-order absorption with lag | -- | Results, 'Pharmacokinetics of lumefantrine'; Methods (ADVAN4 TRANS4) |
| `lka` | log(0.032 1/h) | Table 2, Ka |
| `lvc` | log(25.6 L) | Table 2, Vc/F |
| `lcl` | log(4.54 L/h) | Table 2, CL/F |
| `lq` | log(1.23 L/h) | Table 2, Q/F |
| `lvp` | log(203 L) | Table 2, Vp/F |
| `ltlag` | log(1.45 h) | Table 2, t lag |
| `lfdepot` | fixed(log(1)) | Table 2, F1 (fixed); Methods |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | fixed 0.75, 1 | Methods, allometric formula (70 kg reference; not on Ka or tlag) |
| `e_efv_fdepot` | 0.42 | Table 2, F1 EFV |
| `e_nvp_fdepot` | 1.32 | Table 2, F1 NEV |
| `etalka`, `etalvc`, `etalq`, `etalvp`, `etalfdepot` | log(CV^2 + 1) of 29%, 82%, 27%, 39%, 47% | Table 2, BSV column; Methods (exponential random effects) |
| `etaiov_cl_1` ... `etaiov_cl_6` | log(0.19^2 + 1) | Table 2, BOV column on CL/F |
| `addSd` | 26.30 ng/mL | Table 2, ADD |
| `propSd` | 0.083 | Table 2, PROP |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | ng/mL | Dose in mg, volume in L |

# Typical-value checks

For a 70 kg patient with no random effects, the model is linear, so the
AUC from zero to infinity after the six doses equals F x total dose / CL. The
check below solves the typical patient in each arm and compares the PKNCA
AUC0-inf with that closed form.

```{r typical}
dose_times <- function(ndays) {
  unlist(lapply(seq_len(ndays) - 1, function(d) if (d == 0) c(0, 8) else c(24 * d, 24 * d + 12)))
}
# One occasion per AL dose; held at 6 after the sixth dose.
occ_of <- function(t, dt) pmin(findInterval(t, dt), 6L)

obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 72, 1), seq(72, 180, 4), seq(100, 120, 1), seq(150, 170, 1),
  seq(192, 1500, 48), 168
)))

make_subject <- function(id, ndays, amt, wt, efv, nvp, obs = obs_grid) {
  dt <- dose_times(ndays)
  d <- data.frame(id = id, time = dt, amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  o <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  x <- dplyr::bind_rows(d, o) |> dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  x$WT <- wt
  x$CONMED_EFV <- efv
  x$CONMED_NVP <- nvp
  x$OCC <- occ_of(x$time, dt)
  x
}

typ_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_subject(1, 3, 480, 70, 0, 0) |> mutate(arm = "Control"),
  make_subject(2, 3, 480, 70, 0, 1) |> mutate(arm = "NVP"),
  make_subject(3, 3, 480, 70, 1, 0) |> mutate(arm = "EFV")
)
# Three typical patients solved together; rxode2 warns that a multi-subject
# solve has no omega, which is intended here.
typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui, "omega"), typ_ev, keep = "arm",
                  returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)

typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::filter(typ, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
typ_auc <- as.data.frame(typ_nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f_rel = c(Control = 1, NVP = 1.32, EFV = 0.42)[arm],
    closed_form = f_rel * 6 * 480 / 4.54 * 1000,
    pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - closed_form) / closed_form
  )
typ_auc |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPORRES, closed_form, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "PKNCA AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = PPORRES,
    "F x dose / CL (ng*h/mL)" = closed_form, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2))
# The only difference is the trapezoid and the extrapolation past 1500 h.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_auc$pct_diff) < 2))
```

# Virtual cohort

Each arm is simulated with 200 patients. Body weight is drawn log-normally
around the arm median weight of Table 1 (56, 55 and 58 kg for control, NVP and
EFV) and truncated to the 36-92 kg span the table reports. The four EFV
regimens reuse one cohort (same weights and random-effect draws), so the
regimen comparison is not blurred by sampling differences between cohorts.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200
draw_wt <- function(n, med, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(med), 0.2)), 36), 92)
}
scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,          ~ndays, ~amt, ~efv, ~nvp, ~wt_med, ~seed,
  "Control 480 bid 3d",   3,  480,    0,    0,     56,    1,
  "NVP 480 bid 3d",       3,  480,    0,    1,     55,    2,
  "EFV 480 bid 3d",       3,  480,    1,    0,     58,    3,
  "EFV 480 bid 5d",       5,  480,    1,    0,     58,    3,
  "EFV 480 bid 7d",       7,  480,    1,    0,     58,    3,
  "EFV 1200 bid 3d",      3, 1200,    1,    0,     58,    3
)

sim_one <- function(row) {
  wt <- draw_wt(n_per_arm, row$wt_med, row$seed)
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per_arm), function(i) {
    make_subject(i, row$ndays, row$amt, wt[i], row$efv, row$nvp)
  }))
  # Same rxode2 seed for the shared EFV cohort, so its random effects match.
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(100 + row$seed)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out$scenario <- row$scenario
  dplyr::select(out, id, time, Cc, sim, scenario)
}
sims <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(k) sim_one(scenarios[k, ])))
sims$scenario <- factor(sims$scenario, levels = scenarios$scenario)
```

# Concentration-time profiles (Figure 3)

```{r figure3, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("NVP 480 bid 3d", "EFV 480 bid 3d", "Control 480 bid 3d"),
                time >= 48, time <= 336) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(p05, 10), ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Lumefantrine (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles with residual error; replicates Figure 3 of Maganda 2015.")
```

# PKNCA and comparison with Table 3

Maganda 2015 Table 3 reports the median (IQR) of simulated Cmax, AUC0-inf,
Tmax and day-7 concentration. PKNCA is run on the individual predictions
(no residual error) of each simulated patient over 0 to infinity; the day-7
concentration is read off the profile at 168 h after the first dose.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sims |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, scenario)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | scenario + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs"))
day7 <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 168) |>
  dplyr::transmute(scenario, id, PPTESTCD = "c168", PPORRES = Cc)
pk_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(nca_res, day7)

sim_summary <- pk_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES), q1 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.25), q3 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Table 3 medians and quartiles (Tmax has no 5-day, 7-day or 1200 mg values).
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,            ~PPTESTCD,    ~PPORRES,  ~pub_q1,  ~pub_q3,
  "Control 480 bid 3d", "cmax",         8192.7,   5664.3,  11896.8,
  "NVP 480 bid 3d",     "cmax",        10229,     7173.4,  14606,
  "EFV 480 bid 3d",     "cmax",         3182.2,   2198.4,   4586.1,
  "EFV 480 bid 5d",     "cmax",         3678.2,   2609.7,   5150.7,
  "EFV 480 bid 7d",     "cmax",         3887.5,   2690.4,   5531.4,
  "EFV 1200 bid 3d",    "cmax",         7955,     5496.2,  11464,
  "Control 480 bid 3d", "aucinf.obs", 784830,   547405,  1116250,
  "NVP 480 bid 3d",     "aucinf.obs", 977645,   688477,  1383975,
  "EFV 480 bid 3d",     "aucinf.obs", 303130,   211080,   431962,
  "EFV 480 bid 5d",     "aucinf.obs", 513760,   359212.5, 713715,
  "EFV 480 bid 7d",     "aucinf.obs", 755090,   528277,  1086525,
  "EFV 1200 bid 3d",    "aucinf.obs", 757835,   527702,  1079925,
  "Control 480 bid 3d", "tmax",           66.1,     63.6,     67.7,
  "NVP 480 bid 3d",     "tmax",           66.1,     60.0,     67.7,
  "EFV 480 bid 3d",     "tmax",           66.1,     60.4,     67.6,
  "Control 480 bid 3d", "c168",          858.7,    562.3,   1333.8,
  "NVP 480 bid 3d",     "c168",         1090.3,    704.4,   1680.4,
  "EFV 480 bid 3d",     "c168",          335.5,    215.8,    519.5,
  "EFV 480 bid 5d",     "c168",         1039.4,    678.1,   1552.8,
  "EFV 480 bid 7d",     "c168",         1079.2,    694.1,   1689.6,
  "EFV 1200 bid 3d",    "c168",          838.9,    539.6,   1298.9
)
param_label <- c(cmax = "Cmax (ng/mL)", aucinf.obs = "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)",
                 tmax = "Tmax (h)", c168 = "Day-7 concentration (ng/mL)")

pk_tbl <- pk_all |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = as.character(scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
# 'c168' (concentration at 168 h) is not a PKNCA code, so its label is set
# after the table is built.
cmp_tbl <- withCallingHandlers(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = pk_tbl,
    reference = dplyr::select(published, scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
    by = "scenario",
    units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", tmax = "h", c168 = "ng/mL")
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("unknown PKNCA code", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
cmp_tbl[["NCA parameter"]] <- sub("^c168 ", "Day-7 concentration ", cmp_tbl[["NCA parameter"]])
knitr::kable(cmp_tbl, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), digits = 1)
```

The interquartile ranges are compared as well, since they depend on the
between-subject and between-occasion variances.

```{r iqr}
fmt <- function(x) format(signif(x, 3), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
cmp <- published |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_summary |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = as.character(scenario)),
                   by = c("scenario", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (median - PPORRES) / PPORRES)
cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD != "tmax") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    PPTESTCD = param_label[PPTESTCD],
    pub_iqr = paste0(fmt(pub_q1), " - ", fmt(pub_q3)),
    sim_iqr = paste0(fmt(q1), " - ", fmt(q3))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, scenario, pub_iqr, sim_iqr) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Published IQR" = pub_iqr, "Simulated IQR" = sim_iqr
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The simulated medians reproduce Table 3 within the sampling noise of a
200-patient arm, with one exception: the day-7 concentration for the 7-day
EFV regimen (starred). On a 7-day regimen the 13th and 14th doses are given at
144 and 156 h, so 168 h is 12 h after the last dose and close to the peak. The
model gives a median near 4,000 ng/mL there, and Figure 4 of the paper agrees:
its day-7 panel places the 7-day regimen near ln(C) = 8.2 (about
3,600 ng/mL), well above every other regimen. The 1,079.2 ng/mL printed in
Table 3 is therefore inconsistent with the paper's own figure; it is
compared here but excluded from the assertion below.

```{r assert}
gate <- cmp |> dplyr::filter(!(scenario == "EFV 480 bid 7d" & PPTESTCD == "c168"))
exposure_diff <- gate$pct_diff[gate$PPTESTCD != "tmax"]
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed CL, F factor, dose or unit moves every median
  # by tens of percent.
  abs(median(exposure_diff)) < 8,
  # Envelope on a robust quantile, not the maximum: the median of a
  # 200-patient arm carries about 6% sampling error, and the draw differs
  # between rxode2 builds and thread counts.
  quantile(abs(exposure_diff), 0.9) < 20,
  all(abs(gate$median[gate$PPTESTCD == "tmax"] - 66.1) < 4)
)
```

# Dose-regimen scenarios for patients on efavirenz (Figure 4)

```{r figure4, fig.height = 4}
fig4 <- pk_all |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "cmax", "c168")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPTESTCD = factor(param_label[PPTESTCD], levels = param_label[c("aucinf.obs", "cmax", "c168")]))
ggplot(fig4, aes(scenario, log(PPORRES))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~PPTESTCD, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Natural log of the parameter",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Maganda 2015.") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Occasion definition.** Table 2 reports between-occasion variability of 19%
  on CL/F but the paper does not say what an occasion was. The model uses one
  occasion per AL dose (`OCC` 1 to 6, held at 6 after the sixth dose, and for
  the longer regimens after their sixth dose), the convention of the related
  Lohy Das 2018 lumefantrine model. The occasion etas share one variance. They
  are not mu-referenced because rxode2 has no occasion level, so they are
  combined through indicator terms; rxode2 prints a warning about this at each
  solve, which has no effect on simulation.
* **Variance scale.** Table 2 gives BSV and BOV as percentages. With the
  exponential random effects stated in Methods they are converted as
  omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1). The simulated IQRs of AUC0-inf and Cmax agree with
  Table 3, which supports this reading.
* **Residual error.** ADD (26.30) and PROP (0.083) are read as standard
  deviations: an additive SD of 26.3 ng/mL sits below the 50 ng/mL LLOQ, and a
  variance reading would give an additive SD of about 5 ng/mL. The paper does
  not state the scale.
* **Random effects fixed to zero.** Table 2 fixes the BSV of CL/F and of the lag
  time to 0, so these carry no between-subject eta.
* **Covariates on clearance.** The full model also had ART-arm effects on CL/F
  (Figure 2, CLARM1 and CLARM2); the final model kept only the bioavailability
  effects, and only those are encoded.
* **Virtual weights.** Table 1 labels its weight brackets as IQRs, but they span
  36-92 kg and look like ranges. Weights are drawn log-normally (SD 0.2 on the
  log scale) around the arm medians and truncated to that span.
* **Day 7.** The day-7 concentration is taken at 168 h after the first dose, for
  every regimen.
* **Table 3, 7-day regimen.** See the comparison section: the printed day-7
  median for 7-day dosing contradicts Figure 4 and the model.
* No erratum was found for this article (Europe PMC, checked 2026-11-24). The
  paper has no supplementary material.
